## Session 10: score what the organisers score (2026-10-12 11:42 UTC to 2026-10-13 13:00 UTC)

Rashad's instructions, run unattended by Claude Code; status in `docs/session_10_status.md`, report in
`docs/session_10_report.md`. Branch `rashad/session-10` from `main` at `42b2a3c` (PR #16 merged); a draft pull
request, never merged, no tag. Model: the 8B named in `.env` on Public AI only, at most one request per second,
one model run at a time. Sealed: the test rows dated 2020-02-09, 2022-02-13 and 2022-05-15 are never run,
parsed or opened; `data/test/`, the splits file and the scorer stay unchanged.

- **Branch from `main` at `42b2a3c`.** Rashad's instruction ("from a fresh main").
- **Step 0: `docs/official_scoring.md` restates the organisers' Q&A slides of 8 October in our words; CLAUDE.md's scoring section, the minimum Macro-F1 (0.60 A, 0.75 B; the starter at `5e695772` says 0.70 for B, our bar stays 0.75), the published-image run and the separate containers are corrected; the open question on the formula is removed.** Rashad's instruction; the slides are the newer source.
- **REF SCORE counts tokens per case as input plus output tokens.** The proxy counts "tokens" and the slides do not say whether output counts; counting both is the stricter reading, and every run also reports input and output separately.
- **REF SCORE marks a task below its minimum as invalid and sets the total to 0.** The slides: below either minimum the whole submission is invalid.
- **Step 1: local time is measured in the image with `--cpus 2 --memory 4g`, a read-only root, /tmp as tmpfs, the data read-only and the host network, against the fake model in this process (`scripts/local_time.py`).** The organisers' hardware is unknown; 2 CPUs and 4 GB are session 8's speed-check setting, so the numbers compare with it. The fake model answers every request after a fixed delay (1.0 s, then 0.3 s) with the saved real answer (replay), so the run takes the real path.
- **Local time is measured with the page cache warm (one short warm-up run first).** The first run after the Docker daemon starts read the image's 470 MB model file from a slow disk: one task B case took 54 s instead of 10 s. That is the sandbox's disk, not the pipeline; the cold first run is reported once as a note.
- **The fake model's log marks a request "in flight" from the moment its headers have arrived to the moment its answer has been written.** That is what a proxy in front of the model can see; connection set-up before the request arrives is local time (measured separately on the real endpoint).
- **Step 2: `predict()` is split into `prepare()` (all local work: booklet, routing, embedding, messages) and `complete()` (the model call and the response); `predict()` = `complete(prepare())` is the sequential path, kept as `--workers 0`.** The requests do not change, so G1 and G2 against the session 9 reference must hold for both paths (they do).
- **Step 2: the cases are prepared in one forked worker process, not in threads.** With two threads, PDF reading (pure Python) and the creation of the ONNX session (which holds Python's lock for up to 2.45 s, measured in the container) kept the thread that sends requests waiting: task B's second request left 7.6 s late, and two threads reading two booklets at once doubled task A's time to the first request (3.4 to 6.3 s). A process has its own lock. One process, not two: each process has its own caches, so two would read most booklets twice.
- **Step 2: preparation order = cases needing no local model first, then grouped by booklet in order of first appearance.** Task B: the first requests go out while the e5 model loads. Task A: each booklet's later cases are ready as soon as it is read, so the queue rarely runs dry; in input order the first 25 cases each needed a new booklet. The order of work never changes a request.
- **Step 2: one kept connection per thread (`requests.Session`); a connection error is sent once more on a new connection.** Measured on the real endpoint: 486 ms set-up per call with a new connection against 1.2 ms with a kept one. A kept connection the server closed shows up as a connection error, so one resend on a fresh connection is needed; before, a connection error was never retried.
- **Step 2: ONNX threads = the container's CPU limit (cgroup), not the machine's cores.** In a 2-CPU container on 4 cores, 2 threads embedded 124 paragraphs in 9.5-10.1 s against 11.3-12.5 s; the vectors are bit-identical for 1, 2 and 4 threads (checked on 124 paragraphs).
- **Step 2: `booklet.parse` is cached per booklet text; pages are kept in memory per booklet; pypdf is imported on first use; `src/` is compiled when the image is built.** All are the same computation done once instead of per case (booklet.parse cost about 33 ms on every case).
- **Step 3: the publish workflow's token has `contents: read` and `packages: write`.** "Write permission for packages only": checkout needs read access to the repository; no other write permission is granted.
- **Step 3: the published image is checked inside the workflow (a second job pulls it by its commit tag on a fresh runner and runs the organisers' command against the fake model without internet).** The sandbox cannot use the workflow's token; an anonymous pull from the sandbox also worked (the package is public), and the pulled image answered both examples.
- **Step 2 adopted under the same-answer rule.** G1 and G2 hold against the session 9 reference (both the default and `--workers 0`; tests pass), and local time per case falls for both tasks at both delays (A 0.803 → 0.015 s at 1.0 s per request, 0.742 → 0.300 s at 0.3 s; B 0.985 → 0.008 s, 0.939 → 0.470 s with the cut).
- **Step 2: task B's default is the whole reference again (no cut).** B-cut still costs local time when the model is fast (0.470 s per case at 0.3 s per request against 0.009 s without it). The two measured delays disagree under REF SCORE (B-cut higher at 1.0 s, no cut higher at 0.3 s), so the mean S_B over both delays decides: no cut, dev 0.827 vs 0.821, val 0.821 vs 0.817. Reading: the rule says "higher S_B"; with two measured times, their mean is the reading that does not pick a model speed we cannot know. B-cut stays in the code (`--context-b cut`).
- **Step 2: one worker process by default, not two.** Each process has its own caches; two would read most booklets twice. A second process with booklets assigned to it (task A at 0.3 s per request is limited by one process reading PDFs: 0.30 s per case) is left for later.
- **Step 4: the probe's lines are chosen as text before any parsing.** A task A line is parsed only if it names a probe date's booklet path; the task B lines and expected labels are picked by the probe rows' ids as text. So no line of a sealed date is ever parsed. The booklet URLs come from the parquet's three booklet columns only (date, language, URL), filtered to the probe dates.
- **Step 4: the probe runs through the image with the organisers' command, task A and task B in separate containers.** That is how the organisers run it (docs/official_scoring.md).
- **Step 4: the parser gap found on the probe (`2025_09_28_fr`, vote 1: contents entry without arguments) is reported, not fixed in this step.** The probe "may be used like dev" only from now on; a parser change would need its own check on dev and val (G1/G2 for the booklets it does not concern).
- **Step 5: the new short prompts use the dataset README's label names word for word: "Entailment (0)", "Unrelated / Neutral (1)", "Contradiction (2)".** The README (commit `fc2b2760`, 2026-10-08 12:40 UTC) now defines `entailment_label` as "The entailment class of the `claim` relative to the `reference_string` and voting booklet as a whole. May be `Entailment` (`0`), `Unrelated / Neutral` (`1`) or `Contradiction` (`2`)." CLAUDE.md asks to quote the definitions once they appear; the label names are the definition's content, and the whole sentence would not fit P-short's 200 tokens. The current defaults keep their wording (a prompt change needs its own comparison).
- **Step 5: "fixed text" = the system prompt plus the user message's labels (`PART:`, `REFERENCE TEXT:`, `VOTE:`, `CLAIM:`), counted with the Apertus v1 tokenizer.** P-short (`A-v5-short`): 184 + 16 = 200 tokens (today 314 + 16); BP-short (`v6-short`): 135 + 9 = 144 (today 194 + 9). The PART line's text is per route and unchanged.
- **Step 5: P-short applies to routed cases only; a case that falls back to embed-e5-small keeps its prompt.** Routed cases are 99 % of dev; the fallback prompt is a different prompt for page excerpts.
- **Step 5: B-cut4 ranks paragraphs with e5, as B-cut does.** "Most similar" means what it meant in session 9; its local time is measured and enters its REF SCORE.
- **Step 8: a vote name the title match cannot place is placed by meaning (e5) if the closest title leads the second by at least 0.04; adopted (G1 and G2 unchanged on dev and val).** With the same votes' names from the other languages swapped in for all 880 dev and val cases (votes aligned by order in the contents), the largest lead of a wrong pick was 0.0296; 0.04 keeps a buffer and places 182 of 264 swapped names right, none wrong. Booklets with a single vote are never placed by meaning. Found while testing: names of votes that are not in the booklet at all (5,220 names of other dates' votes) are placed in 649 cases at 0.04, and no threshold on the lead or on the similarity separates them from right picks with useful coverage (best similarities overlap: right picks 0.80-0.93, absent names up to 0.93). In the dataset the vote always belongs to the booklet, and before step 8 such a case fell back to embed-e5-small, which reads the whole booklet; the risk is recorded, not engineered away.
- **Step 5, task A: K4 fails the TOKEN RULE on val (Macro-F1 0.944 vs 0.959, evidence 0.938 vs 0.955); P-short (0.670 on dev) and P-short+K4 (0.619) fail on dev. No task A version is adopted; there is no K6 run (the instruction's K6 run was for a K4 that fails on dev).**
- **Step 5: a version that passes the TOKEN RULE is adopted only if it does not lower REF SCORE, mean over the two measured delays.** The TOKEN RULE does not see local time, and two of the four versions (K4, B-cut4) buy their tokens with e5 work in the background; the session's aim is to score what the organisers score. (No version reached this check: K4 failed on val first.)
- **Step 7: 100 dev task A cases (every third case), today vs the same prompt without response_format; 0 of 100 answers unreadable (rule: more than 2 % would need a more tolerant reader), Macro-F1 0.980 vs 0.969, +1.3 output tokens. Nothing changes.** Task B sends no response_format by default, so it has nothing to compare and got no run.
- **Step 6: the endpoint enforces a schema with anyOf (5 requests: 2 ordinary, 3 told to answer a forbidden combination; all 5 answers schema-conformant), so CS runs.**
- **Step 6: the on-topic neutral set removes every paragraph that overlaps the gold passage, by either of two tests (partial ratio ≥ 90 either way, or any 60-character window of the paragraph inside the passage), before section-route's length cut; a case is kept with at least three paragraphs left (46 of 200).** "Overlapping" must also catch a paragraph that holds only part of the passage; removing too much only makes the expected neutral surer. The set runs through a test-only option of the run script, so `src/` is unchanged.
- **Step 6: CS fails rule (d) on dev (on-topic neutral share 0.609 vs 0.674, more than 0.05 below) and gains nothing on dev (1 fix, 1 break), so SL is the better one and goes to val alone.**
- **Step 6: SL fails the PAIRED RULE: val +0.0034 (needs +0.005) and over dev and val 3 fixes, 0 breaks, sign test p = 0.25 (needs ≤ 0.10). Both stay in the code, off. Nothing changes.**
- **Step 6: the Python rule "neutral with a citation → contradiction" is scored offline only, from today's saved answers (dev, on-topic set, val); it is not in `src/`.** Rashad's instruction: every label comes from an answer of Apertus.
- **Two worker processes ("lanes"), each owning whole booklets, are the default (one on a single CPU).** Same answers (G1 and G2 pass). Local time per case for task A: 0.206 s against 0.316 s with one lane at 0.3 s per request; 0.018 s against 0.015 s at 1.0 s per request, where both are below REF SCORE's 0.05 s, so T_A is 1.0 either way. The same-answer rule asks local time to fall for both tasks; read as the mean over the two measured delays, task A's falls (0.166 → 0.112 s) and task B's cannot change (task B has no booklets and runs in one lane: 0.007 / 0.008 s). Peak memory 2.3 GB of 4 GB. Running the lanes at a lower CPU priority did not remove the small cost at 1.0 s and was taken out again.
- **Step 5, task B: BP-short fails on dev (0.667, 29 unreadable answers); B-cut4 passes the TOKEN RULE on dev (0.987 vs 0.967, −56 % input tokens) and val (0.961 vs 0.957, −54 %), the only qualifying version; it is not adopted because it lowers REF SCORE, mean over both delays (dev 0.832 vs 0.843, val 0.812 vs 0.837): its e5 embedding costs 0.066 s local time per case at 1.0 s per request and 0.730 s at 0.3 s, against 0.0075 / 0.0067 s today.** The rule recorded at step 5 before any task B run. The comparison is close at 1.0 s and depends on the other teams' best local time (break-even about 0.027 s per case).
- **Step 9 (optional): B-U is not adopted and not run on val.** On dev 0.976 vs 0.967 (7 fixes, 4 breaks) with −30 % input tokens, but +5.6 output tokens per case (the answer names paragraphs), and "no version may add output tokens"; its cut text needs e5 like B-cut, so REF SCORE (mean over both delays, B-cut's measured local time) is 0.816 against today's 0.843. Reading: the rule on output tokens holds for every version, not only step 2's.
- **FINISH: the final defaults are those after step 2 and step 8, plus the two lanes; steps 5, 6, 7 and 9 change no default.**
- **FINISH: the final runs use the image the publish workflow built and pushed (`ghcr.io/rashad18236/hackapertus-voting-nli:sha-421d8c804677`, pulled anonymously), not a sandbox build, with task A and task B in separate containers.** That is the artefact the organisers pull, run the way they run it; `src/`, `Dockerfile` and `requirements.txt` are unchanged since `421d8c8`.
- **FINISH: val task B uses `output/valB/cases.jsonl` (the task B cases of the 580 val rows, as in session 9 and step 5); "580 val both tasks" reads as these 580 plus `data/val/`'s 580 task A cases.** `data/val/` holds task A cases only.

## Robustness experiments: cross-language tournament, negation, decomposition, retrievers (2026-10-12, from 12:30 UTC)

Kaan's experiments, with Claude Code. Branch `kaan/robustness-experiments` from `main` at `42b2a3c`. Report:
`docs/robustness_experiments.md`. Everything new is off by default; no default was changed. The test split
was never used.

- **Four ideas, each a switch, compared in one interleaved run against today's defaults.** Kaan's request: try the cross-language tournament, the negation check, claim decomposition and other retrievers, each on its own, with results per variant.
- **Model calls run alongside session 10, one request every 2 s (`--min-interval 2`).** Kaan's choice ("run now, slowly"); half of session 10's rate, so the two together stay at the rate session 10 used alone.
- **Translation is local (facebook/m2m100_418M, MIT, CTranslate2 int8), not Apertus.** Kaan's choice: no tokens for translation; one model covers all six directions (opus-mt has no French-to-Italian model). Its time counts as local time, which the organisers score (T).
- **The MT packages go into `requirements-experiments.txt`, not `requirements.txt`.** The Docker image stays the submission until a variant is adopted.
- **A strategy keeps today's request as its building block (`judge`), and records every sub-answer.** Then the strategies differ only in what they ask, and other combination rules can be computed offline from the saved answers at no token cost (`scripts/strategy_analysis.py`).
- **Strategies apply to routed task A cases and to task B; the fallback path (about 1 in 300 dev cases) stays a single call.** The fallback answers pages, not paragraphs; covering it would double the code for almost no cases.
- **Tournament: both sides agree → that label, else one tie-break call with today's request.** Kaan: "only if both sides align we conclude"; the tie-break keeps a disagreement from turning into a guess.
- **Negation: a neutral answer is replaced by the label the negation implies; otherwise today's answer stays.** Most task A errors are supported or refuted claims called neutral; a rule that also overrides entailment and contradiction would risk the cases that are right today. Alternatives are scored offline.
- **Decomposition only for claims of at least 180 characters (about a quarter of dev claims), each part judged by its own call.** Shorter claims are mostly one fact; one call per part reuses the tested prompt instead of a new multi-claim prompt.
- **Retrievers: BM25 (pure Python), BM25 on the claim translated into the booklet's language, reciprocal-rank fusion with e5, and that fusion on the vote's pages; all on embed-e5-small's chunks with its prompt.** Only the ranking differs, so the comparison is about retrieval alone.
- **Retrieval is measured first offline (gold passage among the sent chunks, `scripts/retrieval_check.py`, no tokens), then with the model with routing off.** Routing already sends the gold passage in 200 of 200 routed dev cases, so retrievers matter for the cases routing cannot handle; running them alone shows what such a case would get.
- **The booklet's language for bm25-mt is detected from its text (`src/langid.py`).** The context variants' interface does not pass the request's language fields; detection also copes with a wrong field.
- **No new variant becomes a default here.** Adoption needs a val confirmation and the token/time trade-off under the official formula; that is a separate decision.
- **At the merge with `main` (sessions 10 and 11), `main`'s `src/cli.py` was taken unchanged and the `--strategy-a/-b` hooks were dropped.** `main` turned `src/cli.py` into a prepare-then-run pipeline; the strategies were measured and not adopted, so porting their hooks would add code for nothing. The runs' code is commit `95588ed`; `src/strategies.py` and its tests stay. The retriever variants need no hook (context registry) and still run with `--context-a`.
